skills: Year 1
Spreadsheets properly, before MSC 221 Computer Applications in Business: formulas, absolute references, lookups, pivot tables, one chart that makes one point.
Business writing that gets to the point: ENG 101 and ENG 102 first, then BUS 201 Business Communication (printed with the Business Core, counted in GenEd).
The accounting equation and the three statements from ACT 201 Financial Accounting - on a real annual report, not only the textbook.
Presenting a case for five minutes without reading, from BUS 102 Business - Basics, Ethics and Environment onward.
Year 2
Reading an annual report and computing its ratios (ACT 202 Management Accounting, FIN 201 Financial Environment and Banking).
Statistics and quantitative methods you can run and explain (STA 101, BUS 209 Quantitative Methods for Business, MSC 221).
Micro and macro as tools for a business decision - ECO 101 and ECO 102, the Allied pair the Department of Economics and Social Sciences teaches.
Working in a team that delivers: roles, deadlines, one version of the file (MGT 213 Management Practices and Organizational Behavior).
Year 3
A research project from question to report in BUS 302 Research Methods and Business Analytics - the gate, with MSC 321, to every analytics, e-business and operations major course.
Case analysis with a recommendation and numbers behind it (MKT 301 Marketing Management, BUS 301 International Business, FIN 301 Financial Management).
What a business actually records and runs: MSC 321 Management Information Systems and MSC 301 Production and Operations Management.
A CV, a LinkedIn profile and two people in your target industry you can ask for advice - the BUS 400 search starts here.
Year 4
Strategy: seeing the whole firm at once in MGT 480 Business Strategy, the capstone with eight printed prerequisites.
Six major courses that tell one story - and, if you want a minor, the two MM courses of a second area.
An internship report or a thesis (BUS 400) you would show an employer.
Interview practice: your story, three achievements with numbers, two questions for them.
dept.career_intro: A BBA is read by employers through its major, its internship and its CGPA - in roughly that order once you are past the first screening. The curriculum prints eight major areas and the programme page lists Accounting, Finance, E-Business, Entrepreneurship, Human Resource Management, Information Systems, Management, Marketing and Operations and Supply Chain Management as specialisations. The table lists where each usually leads; none of it is a BRACU rule.

Audit and assurance firms, corporate accounts and finance departments, internal audit, tax.
The Accounting major (ACT 301, ACT 422, ACT 427 Auditing and Assurance, ACT 431), ACT 423 Fundamentals of Taxation, spreadsheets, a professional-qualification plan.

Banks, non-bank financial institutions, capital-market firms, corporate treasury, insurance.

The Entrepreneurship major (BUS 421 Venture Development, BUS 422, FIN 422, MKT 428), BUS 423 Business Plan Development, a venture you actually ran; the Entrepreneurship Forum (BUEDF).

career_notes: Major, dual major, General Business and the minor

The curriculum prints eight major areas, each four mandatory courses (two marked MM, two marked M) plus two electives (E). 'Students may choose to specialize in multiple areas', and may 'opt to major in General Business by taking 6 courses from any of the BBA major compulsory or elective courses'. In a dual major a course listed in two areas counts for one only - the PDF's example is MSC 446 Marketing on the Internet, which counts for E-Business, where it is mandatory, not Marketing. The 9-credit block after the major is one of three things: a minor in a second area (its two MM courses plus one more from its list), 'any three 300/400-level courses from any of the BRACU courses' with no minor, or a minor from another school or department whose credit requirement 'can be different'.

BUS 400 Internship/Thesis (4 credits) 'is a mandatory requirement for all graduating students': a trimester placed in an organisation, then a report and a presentation under a BRAC Business School faculty supervisor. The thesis alternative needs a minimum CGPA of 3.25 in section 3.6 of the curriculum - the structure table's footnote says 3.5 - plus at least one trimester of supervised research, a thesis paper and a presentation, and it may run longer than a trimester. The OBE Master File codes the same course BUS 490. The programme page lists OCSAR among the services open to you - ask it about placements a year ahead.

facts: Structure (SU25 PDF): General Education 13 courses / 39 credits (Stream 1 Writing 6, Stream 2 Math and Natural Sciences 6, Stream 3 Arts and Humanities 9, Stream 4 Social Sciences 6, Stream 5 Engaging Communities 3, GenEd Electives 9), Business Core 18 / 54, Allied 2 / 6, Major 6 / 18, Minor / Open Electives 3 / 9, Internship / Thesis 4 = 42 courses, 130 credits.
BUS 201 Business Communication is printed under Business: General but counted in GenEd ("Total 18 courses excluding BUS 201 which is included in GenEd"), so the core is 18 other courses.

Major: four mandatory courses (12 credits) marked MM or M plus two electives (6 credits) marked E in one area; "students may opt to major in General Business by taking 6 courses from any of the BBA major compulsory or elective courses"; students may specialise in multiple areas; dual majors are allowed but a course listed in two areas counts for only one (MSC 446 counts for E-Business, where it is mandatory, not Marketing).

Minor: the area's two MM courses (6 credits) plus one more course from its list (3 credits); or graduate without a minor and take any three 300/400-level BRACU courses; or a minor from another school/department (credits may differ - check with that department).

BUS 400 Internship/Thesis (4 credits) is mandatory for all graduating students: one trimester placed in an organisation, then a report and a presentation under a BRAC Business School faculty supervisor; the thesis alternative needs a minimum CGPA of 3.25 (section 3.6) or 3.5 (structure-table footnote) and at least one trimester of supervised research, and may run longer.
"Students may be required to take non-credit/foundation courses depending on the admission test results"; no codes are printed.

"The list of GenEd courses is subject to changes by the GenEd Program Committee."
Allied course prerequisites are set by the Department of Economics and Social Sciences and may differ from the BBA table.

University rules (Policies and Procedures page): 12 credits or more = full-time; from the 2nd semester the minimum load is 9 credits (4 or more courses) and the maximum 15 credits, or 18 or more only as a special case approved by the Dean/Chairperson and the Registrar; a freshman takes at most 9 credits / 3 courses in the first semester; CGPA below 2.0 means probation (Summer 2022 policy); the OBE file sets a minimum CGPA of 2.00 to graduate and a maximum of 8 years to complete.

book.text: Read this first

This planner puts your whole BBS degree in one place: every published course, the rules that move your CGPA, the dates that cost money, and a working page for every week of the semester - on your phone, offline, with the arithmetic done for you.
What you are holding

items: **Degree** - the Bachelor of Business Administration (BBA) as BRACU prints it: every course, its credits and its prerequisite. Pick a semester and a grade per course and the CGPA, the credit map, the Ready / Locked checks and your semester-by-semester plan follow.
**CGPA** - the grading scale, a quick semester GPA, what it takes to reach a target, a retake what-if on BRACU's own rule, and the CGPA lines that decide waivers and standing.
**Money** - this semester's bill at the published rates, the whole degree roughly, and the dates that cost money with a countdown you can send to your calendar.
**Semester** - deadlines and tasks, your routine with a clash check, and the working pages of a semester (set-up, course pages, check-ins, finals plan), one set per semester.
**Toolkit** - the tools this department's work actually needs, with logs and calculators that count and flag as you type.
**Rules** - BRACU's own grading, retake, probation, load, scholarship and fee rules, with the source named under each.
**More** - clubs and careers, the printable pages, an assignment cover page, the Excel version of the tracker, and your backup.

book.text: What it is not

items: It is **not an official BRACU document**. Nobody at the university wrote, checked or approved it.
It does **not replace your advisor**, your advising sheet or the student portal. Those decide what counts toward your degree.

It is **a snapshot**. Course lists, fees, CGPA lines and dates were read from BRACU's own web pages on 20 October 2026. Universities change these. When a notice and this planner disagree - cross the old line out here, and the notice wins.

book.text: Start in 15 minutes

items: On **Home**, type your name, the semester you were admitted in and the semester you are in now.
On **Degree**, pick the semester and the grade of every course you have passed. Your CGPA appears at once, and every course shows Ready, Locked or Open.
On **Money**, type this semester's fee and drop dates from the Registrar's calendar; they count down on Home.
On **Semester**, put your sections into the routine and your deadlines into the task list.

the Rules tab - Rules that move your CGPA and your money

Most students learn these rules by breaking one. Read them once now. Everything here is taken from BRAC University's published pages as they stood in October 2026; the source is named under each section.
The grading scale
BRAC University's undergraduate scale, in force since Fall 2020. Both A+ and A carry the full 4.0.
A+ to D- are passing grades. F is failing: it earns no credit and counts as zero in your GPA.
How your GPA and CGPA are worked out

Every course gives you **quality points = credits x grade point**. Add the quality points for a semester and divide by the credits you attempted for a letter grade: that is your semester GPA. Do the same across all semesters and you have your CGPA. The policy page prints the same formula: the sum of (grade points x credits) over the credits attempted.
Three things students get wrong

items: **An F stays in the sum until it is retaken.** It adds credits to the bottom of the fraction and nothing to the top.
**A D- passes, but it costs you.** A 3-credit D- is 2.1 quality points against 12.0 for an A - and a grade of B- or below is what the repeat rule exists for.
**W, I, P and AU never enter the GPA.** A W costs you the fee and the semester's work, not grade points.

book.text: Small print

items: This is an independent, unofficial study product. It is not produced by, affiliated with, endorsed by or issued by BRAC University, and it does not use the university's logo, seal or colours.
It is a study aid, not academic advice. Programme structures, fees, scholarship rules and dates change; the Office of the Registrar, your department and your advisor are the authority.
Found something out of date? Cross it out, write in the new figure, and carry on. A planner that is corrected by hand is a planner that is being used.

sheets.title: Internship / thesis milestones (BUS 400)
sheets.blurb: Internship or thesis milestones with countdowns and overdue flags.
sheets.intro: BUS 400 is a trimester in an organisation with a report and a presentation, or a supervised thesis (minimum CGPA 3.25 in section 3.6 of the curriculum, 3.5 in the structure table's footnote). List every milestone with an owner and a due date; the flags show what is slipping.

sheets.intro: One row per group project (or per task inside a big one). The countdown stops when you mark it Submitted; marks roll up into an average at the top.
